summary: Thomas Seymour Burt was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1821–1823). He served as a Major in the Bengal Engineers from 1824 to 1847.

Thomas Walker Arnold studied at Magdalene College under Edward Byles Cowell in 1883. A scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies, he held posts at Aligarh, Lahore, Punjab, the India Office, and SOAS University of London.

Thomas Watters worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Queen's University Belfast and Queen's University of Ireland (1857–1861) and served in HM Diplomatic Service from 1863 to 1895.

Thomas Welbourne Clark studied at Nottingham, Cambridge, and SOAS under Cyril Alexander Rylands, Ralph Lilley Turner, and Walter Sutton Page. An Indology and linguistics scholar, he held lecturing and Reader positions at SOAS and visited UPenn in 1961.

Thomas Wolseley Haig studied at Wellington College and Sandhurst. Working in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1887–1920) and taught at Trinity College, Hartford, and SOAS.
Thomas Zehnder is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Nanking under John Dewey and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Thubten Chodron studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery, under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama and Thubten Yeshe. She served at several Buddhist centers before founding and leading Sravasti Abbey as abbess in 2003.

Thubten Jigme Norbu studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and Professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992).

Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught prominent students including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, Dagpo Rinpoche, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Thubten Samphel studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi (~1973–1978), and Columbia University (~1982–1983). A Tibetology scholar, he held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thubten Yeshe studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Rabten, and Trijang Rinpoche. Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, and taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche studied at Dungkar Monastery and under teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Geshe Rabten, and the 14th Dalai Lama. Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he co-founded Kopan Monastery and served as spiritual director of FPMT.

Thupten Jinpa earned a Geshe Lharam at Ganden Shartse and a B.A. at Cambridge, studying under the 14th Dalai Lama. He taught at Ganden, held research posts at Girton College and Stanford, and founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics.
Thupten Tsering is a scholar in the fields of computational studies and Tibetology. He has held academic posts at Tibet University and the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

Thushini S. Jayawardena works in religious studies and other related fields. She studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka and completed a PhD at Auckland University of Technology in 2017.

Théodore Pavie studied under Eugène Burnouf and Garcin de Tassy. A scholar of Indology and sinology, he succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught at the Catholic University of the West.

Thích Minh Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He served as a Chinese lecturer at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1964) and Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (1964–1975).

Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He pursued his higher education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977) and completing his doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1977.

Tianshu Zhu studied at Northwest University and Ohio State under John C. Huntington. Working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, she held posts at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Korea University, and University of Macau.
